title: Setting Boundaries With a Colleague Who Won't Log Off
script: Sinta: [tired but composed] Yudha, I need to bring something up, and I'd rather do it directly than let it fester any longer.
Yudha: [concerned] Of course, go ahead. You sound like something's genuinely been bothering you for a while.
Sinta: [honest] The messages after nine at night, asking me to review documents or answer questions that could easily wait until morning.
Yudha: [surprised] I hadn't realized it was landing that way. I just tend to send things the moment I think of them.
Sinta: [gentle but firm] I understand that instinct, but receiving them immediately makes it hard for me to actually switch off from work.
Yudha: [reflective] That's fair, and honestly, I wouldn't want someone doing the same to me if our positions were reversed.
Sinta: [practical] Could we agree that anything non-urgent gets scheduled to send the next morning, rather than the instant it comes to mind?
Yudha: [agreeing] That seems entirely reasonable. Most of what I send at night genuinely isn't urgent, if I'm being honest with myself.
Sinta: [appreciative] I appreciate you hearing that without getting defensive, it's not always an easy thing to bring up with a colleague.
Yudha: [thoughtful] I'd rather know directly than have you quietly dreading messages from me every evening.
Sinta: [continuing] There's also the assumption that I'll reply instantly, even outside working hours, which has quietly become the expectation somehow.
Yudha: [conceding] I can see how that builds up over time, even if no single message felt unreasonable on its own.
Sinta: [firm] Exactly, it's the accumulation that wears a person down, not any one particular request.
Yudha: [determined] Going forward, I'll use the scheduled send feature, and I'll try to actually distinguish urgent from merely convenient.
Sinta: [warmly] That would genuinely help. And if something truly can't wait, just say so explicitly, rather than leaving me to guess.
Yudha: [sincere] Understood. Thanks for trusting me enough to say this directly instead of just quietly resenting it.

quiz.question: What specifically bothers Sinta about Yudha's behavior?
options: He never replies to her messages
He sends work messages after nine at night about things that could wait
He talks too much in meetings
He assigns her too many tasks
quiz.explanation: Sinta explains that messages after nine at night asking her to review things could easily wait until morning.

quiz.question: Why does Yudha say he sends messages at that time?
options: He wants to test her responsiveness
He tends to send things the moment he thinks of them
His manager requires it
He forgets during the day
quiz.explanation: Yudha admits he just tends to send things the moment he thinks of them, without considering the timing.

quiz.question: What solution does Sinta propose?
options: Yudha should stop messaging her entirely
Non-urgent messages should be scheduled to send the next morning
She will stop checking messages after work
They should switch to phone calls only
quiz.explanation: Sinta proposes scheduling non-urgent messages to send the next morning instead of immediately.

quiz.question: What deeper issue does Sinta raise beyond the timing itself?
options: Yudha's tone in messages
The assumption that she'll reply instantly outside working hours
Yudha's handwriting
The number of meetings scheduled
quiz.explanation: She raises the assumption that she'll reply instantly even outside working hours, which has become an unspoken expectation.

quiz.question: What does Yudha commit to doing for genuinely urgent matters?
options: Calling her immediately every time
Explicitly stating when something truly can't wait, rather than leaving her to guess
Ignoring urgent matters until morning regardless
Asking a manager to intervene
quiz.explanation: Sinta asks him to say explicitly when something truly can't wait, and Yudha agrees to distinguish urgent from convenient.
